audit.profile_level: Level 1 primary; Level 2 controls evaluated where the repo could answer them and labelled per finding
audit.scope_note: Evaluated sections 4 (container images and build file) and 5 (container runtime) against 4 Dockerfiles, 4 Compose files. Sections 1-3 (62 controls) govern host and daemon state the repository cannot express. Section 6 (2 controls) is operational. Section 7 (9 controls) is Swarm, which this deployment does not use. Copies under .claude/worktrees/ were excluded as agent scratch duplicates of the same files.
audit.re_audit_note: Repository synced from origin/main, 435 commits, before this pass. None of those commits touched an audited file, and no new container, IaC or web-server artifact appeared, so the scope is unchanged. Every evidence line number was re-anchored against the current files; statuses were re-verified rather than carried forward.

findings.title: Ensure that a user for the container has been created

evidence.note: final stage has no USER directive; nginx master process starts as root
no USER directive in the file; Flask server runs as root
no USER directive in the file; server runs as root
compliant - this image drops to a non-root user before CMD

findings.remediation: Add a dedicated non-root user to the three non-compliant images, following the pattern already used in the remote-MCP runner image.
findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/docker/edge-tts-server/Dockerfile
+++ b/docker/edge-tts-server/Dockerfile
@@
 FROM python:3.11-slim
 WORKDIR /app
 RUN pip install --no-cache-dir edge-tts flask flask-cors
 COPY server.py .
+RUN useradd --system --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin appuser \
+    && chown -R appuser:appuser /app
+USER appuser
 EXPOSE 5001
 CMD ["python", "server.py"]
findings.behavior_note: The nginx image binds port 80 as root. Running it unprivileged requires switching to nginx-unprivileged or moving the listener above 1024 and adjusting the published port mapping.

community image on a mutable tag

evidence.note: git is installed but no dependency in requirements.txt is fetched from a git remote
no git+ URLs anywhere in the requirements file

findings.remediation: Drop git from the flux-server apt install unless a transitive pip build requires it. Verify with a clean build before merging.
findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/docker/flux-server/Dockerfile
+++ b/docker/flux-server/Dockerfile
@@
 RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
-    python3 python3-pip python3-dev git \
+    python3 python3-pip python3-dev \
     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
findings.behavior_note: A transitive pip dependency that builds from source could require git. Confirm with a clean build.

findings.title: Ensure Content trust for Docker is Enabled

evidence.note: DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST is not set anywhere in the repo or CI environment

findings.remediation: Set DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1 in build and deploy environments, or adopt digest pinning as the equivalent control for registries without Notary.
findings.behavior_note: Enabling content trust breaks pulls of any unsigned image, which includes most community images used here.

findings.title: Ensure update instructions are not used alone in Dockerfiles

findings.title: Ensure setuid and setgid permissions are removed

evidence.note: no directive removes setuid or setgid bits in any of the four images

findings.remediation: Strip setuid and setgid bits from binaries not required to hold them, as a build step in each image.
findings.behavior_note: Removing setuid indiscriminately can break tooling such as ping or su inside the image. Scope the find to the paths the service actually uses.

findings.title: Ensure that COPY is used instead of ADD in Dockerfiles

findings.title: Ensure secrets are not stored in Dockerfiles

evidence.note: created in this session at the context root, where Docker actually reads it
developer .env files are now excluded from the build context, so local keys stop reaching the image

findings.remediation: Move .dockerignore to the repository root so it applies to the build context actually used, and exclude .env explicitly. Note that REACT_APP_* values are compiled into the client bundle by design, so treat any key placed there as public regardless.
findings.remediation_applied: A root .dockerignore now governs the build context both compose files actually use.

evidence.excerpt: RUN pip install --no-cache-dir edge-tts flask flask-cors
evidence.note: no version pins and no hash verification

findings.title: Ensure that Linux kernel capabilities are restricted within containers

evidence.note: no cap_drop on any service in any of the four compose files; every container keeps Docker's default capability set

findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/docker-compose.yml
+++ b/docker-compose.yml
@@
   pocketbase:
     image: ghcr.io/muchobien/pocketbase:latest
     container_name: alloflow-pocketbase
+    cap_drop:
+      - ALL
findings.behavior_note: The nginx frontend needs CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to bind port 80, and Ollama with GPU access may need additional capabilities. Drop all, then add back per service and test.

findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/desktop/schoolbox/docker-compose.yml
+++ b/desktop/schoolbox/docker-compose.yml
@@
   frontend:
     image: nginx:alpine
+    read_only: true
+    tmpfs:
+      - /var/cache/nginx
+      - /var/run
findings.behavior_note: Every service that writes to its root filesystem will fail to start until its writable paths are mounted as tmpfs or volumes. Roll out one service at a time.

findings.title: Ensure that incoming container traffic is bound to a specific host interface

evidence.note: binds to every host interface, publishing an unauthenticated LLM API to the whole network
the student database is published on all interfaces
same pattern in the schoolbox deployment
compliant - the only mapping in the repo that binds to loopback

findings.remediation: Bind every published port to a specific interface. For a single-box classroom deployment that is loopback plus whatever the frontend needs; only the frontend port should reach the LAN.
findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/docker-compose.yml
+++ b/docker-compose.yml
@@
   pocketbase:
     ports:
-      - "${PB_PORT:-8090}:8090"
+      - "127.0.0.1:${PB_PORT:-8090}:8090"
@@
   ollama:
     ports:
-      - "${OLLAMA_PORT:-11434}:11434"
+      - "127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_PORT:-11434}:11434"
findings.behavior_note: Anything reaching these services from another machine breaks, including a browser talking directly to Ollama or PocketBase rather than through the nginx proxy. The nginx config already proxies all of them, so the in-app path is unaffected.

findings.title: Ensure that the 'on-failure' container restart policy is set to '5'

evidence.note: all 21 service definitions across the four compose files use unless-stopped, which retries indefinitely
same

findings.remediation: Use an on-failure policy with a bounded retry count so a crash-looping service stops rather than restarting forever.
findings.remediation_diff:
--- a/docker-compose.yml
+++ b/docker-compose.yml
@@
   frontend:
-    restart: unless-stopped
+    restart: on-failure:5
findings.behavior_note: unless-stopped restarts a service after a host reboot; on-failure does not. For an appliance-style classroom box that reboot behavior may be wanted, in which case document the deviation rather than changing it.
